BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE SUBODH ABHYANKAR  ON THE 9 th OF MAY, 2025  WRIT PETITION No. 17174 of 2025  AKBAR  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sudhanshu Vyas - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Kusharga Jain- P.L./G.A. for the State.

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India,
seeking the following reliefs:-
"7.1

That, a writ or direction may kindly be issued to the respondent no. 1 to 4 pass appropriate order/ writ for providing administrative cooperation not to interfere in to the peaceful physical possession of the house of the petitioner.

7.2 That, a writ or direction may kindly be issued whereby the respondents authority may be restrained from dismantling the land and building bearing no.88, situated at Village- Bichhadod Khalsa, Tehsil Ghatiya, District Ujjain MP comprised in survey no. PH. No. 59, Land admeasuring 880 square fts belongs to the petitioner.
7.3
That, Issue any other writ, order or direction as this Hon'ble Court deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case."

3] The grievance of the petitioner is that against his son, a case under Section 376 of IPC and other provisions has been registered, which has led the respondents to consider the demolition of the house of such accused persons.

2 WP-17174-2025 4] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has no criminal antecedents, and merely because his son is involved in any criminal activity, his house cannot be demolished without any proper notice.

It is also submitted that the petitioner has come to know Akbar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184679221/
1 about such demolition only by way of a newspaper reporting, in which it is stated that the demolition notices have been affixed on the houses of the concerned accused persons.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, no notice has been affixed on the petitioner's house, but he is apprehending that in such facts and circumstances of the case, his house may be demolished without any justifiable reason.
5] Counsel for the respondents/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.

6 ] Having considered the rival submissions, and on perusal of the record, this Court is inclined to dispose of this petition with a direction to the respondents that before taking any action against the petitioner, an appropriate notice be served to him, so that he can reply, and after passing the order on such reply, the respondents can proceed after a further period of ten days, during which the petitioner can resort to the remedies available to him, under law.
7] With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Akbar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184679221/
